A discussion on damage models in gaming and response animations

Well, it would really make for an interesting game. It would be a game where the player would have to plan their action instead of running into the fray and shrugging off danger because they know they can take on the NPC's or enemies and then heal up back to 100% with a medkit.

There are already steps made in that direction when it comes to non-biological entities, like cars or planes. Making a truly realistic model of the human body and simultaneously tracking hits on each artery and organ by various ammo types and calibers would be a colossal task, however, and only a massive studio could pull that off. Massive studios would never dare making a hardcore game, though, as they're niche by their nature. All these ideas are possible, someone just has to do them. I could see someone making a "realistic body damage" engine and selling it to developers, similarly to how Euphoria ragdolls were used in GTAIV and other games.

The destruction derby games would track damage to specific areas on cars separately, I don't see why this isn't done for characters. IRL Armor and bullet penetration are ranked in levels, there is no reason this can't be put in a game. If a character has armor it shouldn't be a DR value, if the armor successfully stops the weapon or bullet the damage should be negated to transferred to a low amount of blunt force damage.

Yeah, IRL bullets and armor are ranked based on penetration, but when you really start getting in to it you also have to look at all kinds of things like expansion and deflection through all the different parts of the body. Even with armor you can have 22lr slip through and cause serious injury (usually by deflecting from hitting an arm) or without armor have a high powered round go through a torso with little injury.

Honestly having overly-realistic damage models would probably be almost indistinguishable from simply having a very unforgiving model similar to damage models we already have. I think it's less a problem of computing power and more a simulating cost/benefit problem.

It's easy to rank probable tissue damage, temporary cavities, and penetration separately. It always feels like a lost opportunity when I see pistols and SMGs go trough rifle plates and kevlar helmets stop DMR rounds in a game. It's like having an in game assault rifle that only does full auto. Being forced to understand the limits or advantages of an in game weapon and play according to them almost always makes a game more fun. The more it can be a factor the bettor IMO.
